UPSTREAM: ALSA: core api: define offsets for TLV items Currently, there are no pre-defined accessors for the elements in topology TLV data. In the absence of such offsets, the tlv data will have to be decoded using hardwired offset numbers 0-N depending on the type of TLV. This patch defines accessor offsets for the type, length, min and mute/step items in TLV data for DB_SCALE type tlv's. These will be used by drivers to decode the TLV data while loading topology thereby improving code readability. The type and len offsets are common for all TLV types. The min and step/mute offsets are specific to DB_SCALE tlv type. CHROMIUM: drm/i915: Fix divide-by-zero Oops i915 readout doesn't fill all of the various state out and assumes that the first atomic commit it receives is going to be a modeset. In some cases (for R67, it's all cases) Chrome will send a non-modeset commit to the kernel. When the non-modeset commit is received, intel_state is not filled in and has intel_state->active_crtcs == 0. Since readout has determined one crtc is active, we try to calculate the watermark which involves dividing by the number of active crtcs. Since intel_state->active_crtcs == 0, we Oops. This patch fixes exactly that scenario and assumes the rest of the driver will cope with the inconsistent state until we get a modeset. I've got a more general fix for this upstream, but it is much more invasive and given the drift between 3.18 and 4.19, is not guaranteed to work as well here as it does upstream.
